title: The Periodic Table of Languages? A Predictive Stress-Test of Global Circular Organization in Typological Feature Space
domain: linguistic typology / circular seriation / holdout prediction / geometry comparison
summary: Rerun (local ARIS) predictive stress-test of the 'periodic table of languages' claim: six language x feature tables (TLI x3, GBI x2, WALS auxiliary; 555-2,501 languages) under leave-one-family-out (509 executed folds). Pre-registered H1-H4 with margin 0.02 nats/cell. Results: (i) direct circularity diagnostic significant in 4/6 tables (one-sided p <= 0.03, R = 0.049-0.083), ns on TLI_stat_large (p = 0.734) and WALS (p = 0.234, 99.83% imputed); (ii) H1: circular beats marginal baseline on all 3 TLI tables (log-loss 0.4666-0.4857 vs 0.5241-0.5402; sign-test p <= 1.17e-06) but loses on both GBI tables (0.6691/0.6808 vs 0.5410/0.5330; p <= 4.02e-21); (iii) H2 rejected: UPGMA dominates circular on all 5 main tables (family-level 95% CI lower bounds 0.0465-0.1144 above margin), MDS on 3 of 5; (iv) H3 rejected/downgraded - three-layer direction inconsistent (sole outlier source = GBI layer, leave-out-verified) and every layer comprehensively dominated by non-circular comparators. Robustness: leakage guard tightening (|r| 0.90 -> 0.95) no verdict flips; circular strictly worse than pure Macroarea geographic prior on both GBI tables (M5a worse = TRUE); executed random 2-D layout nulls (2 tables) show MDS advantage is not MDS-specific (per-family p = 0.31-0.54). Verdict (claims item 3 phrasing): the periodic structure does not provide holdout predictive power. Provenance: no in-domain indexed source for the claim (OpenAlex negative finding, registered); all data re-fetched + pinned 2026-09-26, all code newly written; M1X double-run byte-identical; M3 xcheck diffs = 0.
